consequential_checks.claim_or_decision: Predictions, measured water levels, verified hourly heights and OFS are distinct products
consequential_checks.analysis: The product identities match NOAA definitions; astronomical predictions remain the primary comparison, observations optional context.

consequential_checks.claim_or_decision: water_level verification depends on availability; datum required in the selected products
consequential_checks.analysis: NOAA water_level can be preliminary or verified; hourly_height is verified. Datum rule is correct for selected level/prediction products; API exempts Air Gap, which is not selected.

consequential_checks.claim_or_decision: Unit and GMT/LST/LST_LDT conventions differ; unknown source time remains unresolved
consequential_checks.analysis: NOAA distinguishes metre/foot units and fixed local standard time from DST-adjusted local time. UTC normalization and unresolved folds/gaps are explicit design/validation policy.

consequential_checks.claim_or_decision: STND is station-unique; subordinate predictions use MLLW; datum labels are not unit conversions
consequential_checks.analysis: The named NOAA datum constraints are correct; equal labels do not supply a local gauge tie.

consequential_checks.claim_or_decision: Metadata resources include datums, superseded datums, sensors/outages, details and offsets
consequential_checks.analysis: Resources and installation/removal fields exist. An available resource is not proof of the selected station historical values; the artifact requires snapshots.

consequential_checks.analysis: The measurement resource describes benchmarks, leveling and geodetic connections. Its landing-page description does not establish the actual local mapping or sufficiency of a benchmark. Final retains that as an owner decision and refuses unsupported residuals.

consequential_checks.claim_or_decision: One public station does not establish equivalence at both volunteer sites
consequential_checks.analysis: A conservative comparability condition, expressly identified as inference. NOAA also describes site-dependent meteorological effects. No selected site/station relationship is empirically established.

consequential_checks.claim_or_decision: Harmonic predictions support dense intervals; subordinate predictions are high/low only
consequential_checks.analysis: The API and help agree on station classifications, offsets and intervals. The proposed event-level alternative is conditional; no invented continuous series is supplied.

consequential_checks.claim_or_decision: Observation and prediction retrieval limits differ
consequential_checks.analysis: Six-minute measured data has a one-month per-request limit. Tide high/low predictions allow ten years and other prediction intervals one year. C4 correctly repairs the broad draft cap; no request was executed as an application witness.

consequential_checks.claim_or_decision: Quarterly prediction updates and live metadata require per-run snapshots
consequential_checks.analysis: NOAA help gives quarterly updates including station upgrades, offsets and reference changes. Snapshot recommendation is justified; these live captures are not historic station records.

consequential_checks.claim_or_decision: Astronomical predictions do not establish weather/runoff effects or a universal accuracy threshold
consequential_checks.analysis: NOAA distinguishes astronomical tides and station-dependent non-tidal effects. Descriptive residuals remain an education product decision.

consequential_checks.claim_or_decision: NOAA RMS table uses prediction-minus-observation differences and one year per station
consequential_checks.analysis: PDF page 1 explicitly describes the sign, RMS and one-year sample; the table contains station analysis years. It is not a two-site one-month threshold. Entire PDF text inspected; relevant first page also visually inspected.

consequential_checks.claim_or_decision: OFS is modeled nowcast/forecast guidance and is rejected as primary reference
consequential_checks.analysis: The source supports product type; excluding it is a justified frozen-scope choice rather than a claim OFS has no value.

consequential_checks.claim_or_decision: API formats and Tide Predictions download/request alternatives
consequential_checks.analysis: CSV/JSON/XML API formats and TXT/XML display downloads plus web-service URLs exist. Offline saved-byte acquisition is a proposed mechanism.

consequential_checks.claim_or_decision: pandas 3.0.6 commit/release and interpreter applicability
consequential_checks.analysis: Independent release JSON dates publication to 2026-09-17; annotated tag resolves to 2905718b126579d2cf0fe5bae05bd75facb67d77. pyproject requires Python >=3.11. Candidate leaves project runtime pin conditional.

consequential_checks.claim_or_decision: merge_asof defaults, sorted time key, by grouping and caller dispatch
consequential_checks.analysis: Public definition defaults backward, exact allowed, tolerance None. Global ascending time key is required; sorting by group alone is not sufficient. Caller constructs _AsOfMerge then gets results; grouped indexers are selected via _asof_by_function.

consequential_checks.claim_or_decision: Compatible tolerance permits zero; finite positive approximate tolerance is policy
consequential_checks.analysis: Validators reject negative values, not mathematical zero; datetime keys still require timedelta-compatible tolerance. Finite positive approximate tolerance is the notebook policy, not a promised pandas validator property.

consequential_checks.claim_or_decision: Compiled as-of joins return row indexers; nearest ties are backward; no interpolation
consequential_checks.analysis: Nearest invokes backward/forward scans and chooses bri on bdiff <= fdiff; public API has no tie override. Tolerance is inclusive. This selects existing right rows, not an estimated height.

consequential_checks.claim_or_decision: Equality default and explicit bounded as-of alternatives are coherent product choices
consequential_checks.analysis: Equality merge is a viable design. Candidate supplies a policy and proposed tests, not runnable merge code. pandas.merge itself defaults inner and can match null keys, so retaining gaps and excluding unresolved times require the stated surrounding policy. No naive-call correctness was claimed; duplicates/cardinality remain implementation acceptance work.

consequential_checks.claim_or_decision: Issue #35558 only proves an incompatible-tolerance diagnostic defect
consequential_checks.analysis: False narrowing. For both index flags, no by keys and non-None compatible tolerance, the parent _get_merge_keys loop has no lk binding. The msg is formatted before any incompatibility branch, so a valid DateTimeIndex/Timedelta call also fails. Issue reports that valid call.

consequential_checks.claim_or_decision: Fix changes lk.dtype to lt.dtype and is released in v1.1.1
consequential_checks.analysis: Patch identity is correct. Immutable fix and release source both carry lt.dtype, release whatsnew records issue 35558, and official release was published 2020-08-20. Shipping is not inferred merely from PR merge.

evidence.range_or_selector: same symbol at release commit f2ca0a2665b2d169c97de87b8e778dbed86aea07, lines 1660-1677

consequential_checks.claim_or_decision: The merged issue-linked result test passes without code changes and misses changed branch
consequential_checks.analysis: The quoted reviewer comment is bound to preliminary commit 59a07c22, whose test has by=ticker and binds lk. Author then replaces it; e7f668b/7214b3c final test has both indexes and no by, valid 0.5-second tolerance, and expected matched result. It reaches the previously failing string construction. Current 3.0.6 test retains that regression setup, skipping second-resolution rounding. Static reachability established; no upstream test run here. General nearest/grouped correctness is still not proven by this single regression.

consequential_checks.claim_or_decision: Historical defect is not automatically current; current source is separately checked
consequential_checks.analysis: Final does not say old UnboundLocalError persists in 3.0.6. The current validator uses lt.dtype and separately checks both actual key dtypes. That release applicability limit is sound despite D1.

consequential_checks.claim_or_decision: Alternatives, rejected leads and eight owner/product choices remain visible
consequential_checks.analysis: All five rejected/limited leads and eight draft product questions remain. Event-only vs unavailable dense series, observations as optional context, static vs interactive plotting, bounded matching/tie choices and optional interpolation are retained. No concrete plotting-library survey or exhaustive opportunity recall is claimed; package choice remains open.
